latest_release.name: v0.169.0
latest_release.body:
The main motivation behind this release is to get out a build with [Go 1.27.3](https://github.com/golang/go/issues?q=milestone%3AGo1.27.3+label%3ACherryPickApproved), which blocks trust in a small set of intermediate certificates due to specific security concerns around their operation. See the [eMudhra incident](https://go.dev/blog/emudhra-incident) for more information. This affects Hugo features that fetch remote resources over HTTPS, e.g. `resources.GetRemote`.

This release also contains some security hardening of the template functions and menu entries that can render content as HTML (see below), a deprecation of looking up reserved front matter fields via `.Params` (also below), a faster and more robust `plainify`, and a set of bug fixes.

## Security notes

Templates are trusted in Hugo, but content (including front matter) is not necessarily. This release tightens a few places where values from content could end up rendered as unescaped HTML:

* `pre` and `post` values in menu entries defined in **front matter** are now HTML escaped, unless `text/html` is allowed in [`security.allowContent`](https://gohugo.io/configuration/security/), which already marks HTML in `/content` as trusted. A warning (`warning-menu-pre-post-html-escaped`) is logged when a value containing HTML markup is escaped. Menu entries defined in the project configuration are not affected. f63482bf
* `emojify` and `plainify` now return a `string` unless the input is `template.HTML`, in which case the result is also `template.HTML`. Previously both always returned `template.HTML`, so e.g. `{{ .Title | emojify }}` would mark a potentially unsafe title as safe HTML. If you relied on the old behavior with trusted input, pipe the result through `safeHTML`. Thanks to @Reload3d for reporting this. #15452

## Deprecations

Reserved front matter fields such as `title`, `date` and `summary` are currently also stored in `.Params`. Lookups such as `.Params.title` (and `ByParam "title"`, `where .Pages "Params.title" ...` etc.) are now redirected to the corresponding `Page` method and logged as deprecated, unless the field was set in the `params` section of front matter. The content of `.Params` is unchanged for now. 53e1fef9

| Deprecated | Use instead |
| --- | --- |
| `.Params.date` | `.Date` |
| `.Params.description` | `.Description` |
| `.Params.draft` | `.Draft` |
| `.Params.expirydate` | `.ExpiryDate` |
| `.Params.keywords` | `.Keywords` |
| `.Params.lastmod` | `.Lastmod` |
| `.Params.layout` | `.Layout` |
| `.Params.linktitle` | `.LinkTitle` |
| `.Params.publishdate` | `.PublishDate` |
| `.Params.slug` | `.Slug` |
| `.Params.summary` | `.RawSummary` (new) |
| `.Params.title` | `.Title` |
| `.Params.translationkey` | `.TranslationKey` |
| `.Params.type` | `.Type` |
| `.Params.weight` | `.Weight` |

## Bug fixes

* hugolib: Fix template change detection when saving via temp file and rename 46e51f30 @bep #15484 
* markup/goldmark: Fix auto heading ID when link text starts with a bracket c22158c1 @chanellebingham #15472 
* urls: Fix JoinPath panic with empty slice ce5d232b @Ferdinand-MZ #15473 
* js: Fix js.Build with browser-disabled extensionless requires 2efee511 @bep #15481 
* Fix Site.Key used in e.g. partialCached b86e0caa @bep #15466 
* ci: Fix Windows running out of disk space and simplify test runs 77230eba @bep 
* hugolib: Fix build hang after too many page render errors 85fb23f1 @bep #15449 
* tpl/cast: Fix nil pointer panic in hugo gen docshelper 8df31809 @jmooring #15444 

## Improvements

* Redirect .Params.title etc. to .Title etc. and deprecate it 53e1fef9 @bep 
* ci: Revert to plain go install honnef.co/go/tools/cmd/staticcheck@latest 3e67572c @bep 
* navigation: Escape pre/post in front matter menu entries f63482bf @bep 
* Upgrade to Go 1.27.3 7343fc9c @bep 
* resources: Make processed image key stable across builds ff4eab75 @bep #15467 
* tpl: Make StripHTML (plainify) more robust and faster

Overview Hugo is a [static site generator][] written in Go, optimized for speed and designed for flexibility. With its advanced templating system and fast asset pipelines, Hugo renders a complete site in seconds, often less. Due to its flexible framework, multilingual support, and powerful taxonomy system, Hugo is widely used to create: - Corporate, government, nonprofit, education, news, event, and project sites - Documentation sites - Image portfolios - Landing pages - Business, professional, and personal blogs - Resumes and CVs Use Hugo's embedded web server during development to instantly see changes to content, structure, behavior, and presentation. Then deploy the site to your host, or push changes to your Git provider for automated builds and deployment. Hugo's fast asset pipelines include: - CSS Processing – Bundle, transform, minify, create source maps, perform SRI hashing, and integrate with PostCSS. - Image processing – Convert, resize, crop, rotate, adjust colors, apply filters, overlay text and images, and extract metadata - JavaScript bundling – Transpile TypeScript and JSX to JavaScript, bundle, tree shake, minify, create source maps, and perform SRI hashing. - Sass processing – Transpile Sass to CSS, bundle, tree shake, minify, create source maps, perform SRI hashing, and integrate with PostCSS - Tailwind CSS processing – Compile Tailwind CSS utility classes into standard CSS, bundle, tree shake, optimize, minify, perform SRI hashing, and integrate with PostCSS And with [Hugo Modules][], you can share content, assets, data, translations, themes, templates, and configuration with other projects via public or private Git repositories. See the [features][] section of the documentation for a comprehensive summary of Hugo's capabilities. ## Sponsors

 

   

## Editions Hugo is available in two editions. Use the standard edition unless you need additional features. Feature|standard|deploy :--|:-:|:-: Core features|:heavy_check_mark:|:heavy_check_mark: Direct cloud deployment (1)|:x:|:heavy_check_mark: (1) Deploy your site directly to a Google Cloud Storage bucket, an AWS S3 bucket, or an Azure Storage container. See [details][]. ## Installation Install Hugo from a [prebuilt binary][], package manager, or package repository. Please see the installation instructions for your operating system: - [macOS][] - [Linux][] - [Windows][] - [DragonFly BSD, FreeBSD, NetBSD, and OpenBSD][] ## Build from source To build Hugo from source you must install: 1. [Git][] 1. [Go][] version 1.27.0 or later ### Standard edition To build and install the standard edition: ```sh CGO_ENABLED=0 go install github.com/gohugoio/hugo@latest ``` ### Deploy edition To build and install the deploy edition: ```sh CGO_ENABLED=0 go install -tags withdeploy github.com/gohugoio/hugo@latest ``` ## Documentation Hugo's [documentation][] includes installation instructions, a quick start guide, conceptual explanations, reference information, and examples. Please submit documentation issues and pull requests to the [documentation repository][]. ## Support Please **do not use the issue queue** for questions or troubleshooting. Unless you are certain that your issue is a software defect, use the [forum][]. Hugo's [forum][] is an active community of users and developers who answer questions, share knowledge, and provide examples. A quick search of over 20,000 topics will often answer your question. Please be sure to read about [requesting help][] before asking your first question. ## Contributing You can contribute to the Hugo project by: - Answering questions on the [forum][] - Improving the [documentation][] - Monitoring the [issue queue][] - Creating or improving [themes][] - Squashing [bugs][] Please submit documentation issues and pull requests to the [documentation repository][]. If you have an idea for an enhancement or new feature, create a new topic on the [forum][] in the "Feature" category. This will help you to: - Determine if the capability already exists - Measure interest - Refine the concept If there is sufficient interest, [create a proposal][]. Do not submit a pull request until the project lead accepts the proposal. For a complete guide to contributing to Hugo, see the [Contribution Guide](CONTRIBUTING.md). ## License For the Hugo source code, see [LICENSE](/LICENSE). We also bundle some libraries in binary/WASM form: - [libwebp](https://github.com/webmproject/libwebp), [BSD-3-Clause license](https://github.com/webmproject/libwebp?tab=BSD-3-Clause-1-ov-file#readme) - [Katex](https://github.com/KaTeX/KaTeX), [MIT license](https://github.com/KaTeX/KaTeX?tab=MIT-1-ov-file#readme) - [QuickJS](https://github.com/bellard/quickjs?tab=License-1-ov-file#readme), [License](https://github.com/bellard/quickjs?tab=License-1-ov-file#readme)
